title: Cohomology and quotient maps of a two-term integral coefficient complex
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field, and $X=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Work on a small skeleton of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ in the coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p_X^*$ be the inverse image from the condensed point [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], and put $R=p_X^*\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$ and $B_n=p_X^*\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z}$ for $n\ge1$, with their quotient maps. The underlined rings are the continuous-function condensed rings, and these are the pulled-back coefficient rings [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the canonical finite discrete ring identifications of [lem-pe-condensed-point-discrete-constant-comparisons]. Let $k_X$ be the constant $\mathbf F_\ell$-module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], acted on by $B_n$ through reduction modulo $\ell$. Use sheaf modules and sheaf tensor [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

Let $P=[R\xrightarrow{\ell}R]$ in cochain degrees $-1,0$, zero elsewhere [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and $K=Q_R(P)$ in the unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $P$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], its derived reduction $K_n=K\otimes_R^L B_n$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] is represented by $P_n=[B_n\xrightarrow{\ell}B_n]$, and the canonical quotient transition $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ is represented by reduction in both terms. There are $B_n$-linear identifications
$$H^{-1}(K_n)\cong k_X,\qquad H^0(K_n)\cong k_X,\qquad H^q(K_n)=0\quad(q\notin\{-1,0\}).$$
The first identification is the inverse of the map induced, before $p_X^*$, by $\bar a\mapsto\ell^{n-1}a\bmod\ell^n$; the second is induced by reduction modulo $\ell$. Under these identifications the transition on $H^{-1}$ is zero and the transition on $H^0$ is the identity. Moreover $k_X\ne0$, and the canonical action map is an isomorphism
$$H^{-1}(K_{n+1})\otimes_{B_{n+1}}B_n\xrightarrow{\sim}k_X,$$
where the left side uses sheaf tensor and its map to $k_X$ sends $x\otimes b$ to $\bar b x$ after the specified degree-minus-one identification. Thus the map from this tensor product to $H^{-1}(K_n)$ induced by the quotient transition is zero.

proof.text: For any sheaf of $R$-modules $M$, the maps $m\otimes r\mapsto rm$ and $m\mapsto m\otimes1$ are mutually inverse between $M\otimes_RR$ and $M$: the balanced relation gives $m\otimes r=rm\otimes1$, and the maps extend uniquely through the sheafification defining sheaf tensor. Thus tensoring with $R$ is the identity and tensoring with the zero module is zero; both are exact. The terms of $P$ are therefore flat in the stated sheaf-tensor sense. Since $P^i=0$ for $i>0$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] on the chosen small skeleton to conclude that $P$ is K-flat. This uses no flatness of any quotient ring.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; tensor unit checked directly from sites-modules.tex Tag 03EK

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] to $R\to B_n$ with the identity K-flat resolution $P\to P$. The maps $R\otimes_RB_n\to B_n$, $r\otimes b\mapsto\bar r b$, with inverse $b\mapsto1\otimes b$, identify the resulting complex with $P_n=[B_n\xrightarrow{\ell}B_n]$. These identifications send multiplication by $\ell$ to multiplication by $\ell$. To retain the actual canonical quotient transition, apply [lem-pe-kflat-scalar-tower-realization] with $a_n:R\to B_n$, $b_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$, and $e=1_{Q_R(P)}$. Its flat-term hypothesis was verified in step 1. Its transition equation identifies the canonical derived transition, after scalar restriction, with $p\otimes b\mapsto p\otimes b_n(b)$. Hence in the two nonzero terms it is precisely $b_n$, not a choice of a chain map with the same source and target.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; specified quotient-transition refinement in lem-pe-kflat-scalar-tower-realization

proof.text: Put $A_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ and $k=\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z=\mathbf F_\ell$. Since $\Omega$ is algebraically closed, hence separably closed, and each $A_n$ and $k$ is a discrete ring, [lem-pe-condensed-point-discrete-constant-comparisons] gives isomorphisms of internal rings, retaining multiplication and unit, $\varphi_n:B_n\xrightarrow{\sim}(A_n)_X$ and $\varphi:p_X^*\underline k\xrightarrow{\sim}k_X$ onto the constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]; on the test objects $X[S]$ their sections are $LC(S,A_n)$ by [det-pe-condensed-point-coefficients]. The quotient map $b_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$ is $p_X^*$ of the postcomposition morphism $\underline{A_{n+1}}\to\underline{A_n}$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], a ring map by the functoriality of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. The cited lemma does not state naturality of $\varphi_n$ in the ring, so compatibility is checked directly. The ring maps $\varphi_nb_n\varphi_{n+1}^{-1}$ and the constant-sheaf reduction $(A_{n+1})_X\to(A_n)_X$ both preserve units. By the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], a ring map out of $(A_{n+1})_X$ is determined by its restriction to the constant presheaf, that is, by ring homomorphisms $A_{n+1}\to(A_n)_X(U)$. There is only one such homomorphism because $A_{n+1}$ is a quotient of $\mathbf Z$. Hence the two maps are equal, and on $LC(S,-)$ the map is pointwise reduction. The same uniqueness shows the identification does not depend on which comparison isomorphism is chosen. For the kernel inclusion, postcomposition with $u_n:k\to A_n$, $a\mapsto\ell^{n-1}a$ (step 4), is an additive map of condensed abelian groups $\underline k\to\underline{A_n}$ sending $1$ to $\ell^{n-1}\cdot1$. Its image under $p_X^*$, transported by $\varphi$ and $\varphi_n$, and the constant-sheaf map of $u_n$ are additive maps out of $k_X$ that agree on the constant section $1$: the comparisons are additive and send $1$ to $1$, hence $\ell^{n-1}\cdot1$ to $\ell^{n-1}\cdot1$. Since $k$ is generated by $1$ as an abelian group, the two maps agree on the constant presheaf and hence, by the universal property of sheafification, on $k_X$. The same argument applies to the reduction $A_n\to k$. All scalar actions are the ring actions retained by the comparisons. In particular, $u_n$ and reduction are $B_n$-linear when $k_X$ has the residue action.

source.place: Clause (2); canonical comparison on finite coefficients and postcomposition maps

proof.text: Here is the coefficient calculation. For $n\ge1$, define $u_n:k\to A_n$ by $u_n(\bar a)=\ell^{n-1}a\bmod\ell^n$. Changing $a$ by $\ell c$ changes this value by $\ell^nc$, so it is well-defined. It is injective because $\ell^n\mid\ell^{n-1}a$ if and only if $\ell\mid a$. Also $\ell x=0$ in $A_n$ if and only if an integer representative of $x$ is divisible by $\ell^{n-1}$; hence $u_n$ identifies $k$ with $\ker(\ell:A_n\to A_n)$. Reduction $v_n:A_n\to k$ is onto and has kernel $\ell A_n$, since a class reduces to zero exactly when its representative is divisible by $\ell$. Thus $v_n$ induces $\operatorname{coker}(\ell)\cong k$. Both maps are $A_n$-linear when $k$ has its residue action: $\ell^{n-1}(ba)=\ell^{n-1}(\bar b a)\bmod\ell^n$. These statements include $n=1$, when multiplication by $\ell$ is zero and $u_1,v_1$ are identities.

source.place: Final paragraph: explicit elementary coefficient calculation for the non-normalized cohomology witness

proof.text: Apply constant presheaves to the complex $[A_n\xrightarrow{\ell}A_n]$, then sheafify. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], evaluation computes presheaf cohomology and sheafification commutes naturally with cohomology. The additive equivalence [lem-cbc-constant-ring-module-sheaves] identifies these $A_n$-module-valued sheaves with internal modules over the constant $A_n$ ring, retaining the underlying sheaves and maps; thus this is the $B_n$-module complex $P_n$ of steps 2 and 3. Step 4 gives $H^{-1}(P_n)=\ker(\ell)\cong k_X$ via $u_n^{-1}$ and $H^0(P_n)=\operatorname{coker}(\ell)\cong k_X$ via $v_n$. There is no incoming differential at degree $-1$, no outgoing differential at degree $0$, and every other term is zero, so all other cohomology vanishes. The cohomology functors factor through localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], giving exactly the asserted cohomology of $K_n$. The naturality and retained actions give $B_n$-linearity, including the specified map before $p_X^*$ from step 3.

source.place: Tag 093J, lemma-constant-exact; sites.tex Tag 00WJ, lemma-sheafification-exact; module action extension along constant ring sheafification

proof.text: Let $q_n:A_{n+1}\to A_n$ be reduction. On degree-minus-one cycles, $q_nu_{n+1}(\bar a)=q_n(\ell^na)=0$ in $A_n$. Therefore, after the $u_{n+1}^{-1}$ and $u_n^{-1}$ identifications, the induced map is zero. On degree-zero quotients, $v_nq_n=v_{n+1}$ since both send an integer to its residue modulo $\ell$. Therefore the induced map is the identity of $k$. Sheafification preserves these equations, and the functorial kernel/image cohomology construction of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives zero on $H^{-1}$ and identity on $H^0$ for the canonical transition identified in step 2.

source.place: Final paragraph: maps on cohomology computed using the actual quotient map in both terms

proof.text: The identity $X\to X$ is a nonempty pro-etale site object: the zero ideal of the field $\Omega$ is a point of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Apply [lem-sfb-constant-realization-detects-zero] with this object, coefficient ring $k$ and module $k$. It gives an injection $k\to k_X(X)$. Since $\ell$ is prime, $\ell\ge2$ and $0\ne1$ in $k$; their section images are distinct. Thus $k_X\ne0$. This checks nonvanishing without assuming that the integral pulled-back coefficient ring is a discrete constant ring.

source.place: Tags 00WB, theorem-plus, and 00WK, lemma-sections-sheafification; nonempty pro-etale specialization in the cited node

proof.text: Use the identification $H^{-1}(K_{n+1})\cong k_X$ of step 5. Define $\phi:k_X\otimes_{B_{n+1}}B_n\to k_X$ by $x\otimes b\mapsto\bar b x$. It is balanced since both actions factor through $k_X$; it therefore defines a sheaf-module map by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Define $\psi(x)=x\otimes1$. Then $\phi\psi=1$. To check $\psi\phi=1$, take a pure section tensor $x\otimes b$. By [lem-sf-constant-module-unit-locally-bijective], applied to $A_n$ as an $A_n$-module, locally $b$ is a constant $\beta\in A_n$. Choose an integer representative and its class $\widetilde\beta\in A_{n+1}$. The balancing relation gives $x\otimes b=(\widetilde\beta x)\otimes1=(\bar b x)\otimes1$. This is $\psi\phi(x\otimes b)$. Additivity proves equality on each presheaf tensor module locally, the sheaf condition proves equality there globally, and the universal property of sheafification proves equality on the sheaf tensor. The same equation proves $\psi$ is $B_n$-linear; $\phi$ is $B_n$-linear directly. Thus $\phi$ is precisely the asserted action isomorphism. Finally the cohomology transition is zero by step 6, so its balanced map sends $x\otimes b$ to $b\cdot0=0$ and hence is the zero sheaf morphism.
